title: Platform systems & services: dashboards, alerts, runbooks, roadmap, and team wiki (Q2 2026 addendum)
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview:

This document consolidates platform engineering guidance for systems & services: recommended dashboards and alerts, canonical runbooks, operational how-tos, recent retrospectives highlights, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as the single-source playbook for oncall engineers, service owners, and SRE collaborators.

Quick links:
- Team wiki: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q1
- Runbook index: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-runbooks-dashboards-roadmap-2026-q1
- Incident playbook & escalation: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process

Scope and audience:
- Scope: platform-level systems (auth, service mesh, ingress, control plane), shared services (logging, metrics, tracing, alerting, CI/CD), and core runtime services for model inference orchestration.
- Audience: platform engineers, service owners, oncall rotation, solutions engineering, and product ops.

Principles:
1. Reduce blast radius: prefer feature flags, canary rollouts, and circuit breakers for behavioral changes.
2. Observable by default: every service must publish metrics (latency, error rate, saturation), traces for 95th+ p90 flows, and structured logs with request IDs.
3. Runbooks first: every alert must map to a runbook and an owner.

Ownership and oncall:
- Platform oncall: eng-platform team (primary pager for infra/control plane incidents).
- Service owners: teams that deploy to the platform must maintain service-specific runbooks and own long-term fixes.
- Pager rotation: 2-week rotations. See team wiki for current schedule.

SLOs and SLIs (canonical):
- Control plane API (rest-control-plane): availability SLO 99.95% monthly, SLI = successful 2xx responses for management API requests.
- Inference router (ingress/routing service): p99 latency < 150ms for short requests (<= 512 tokens) with availability SLO 99.9% monthly.
- Job scheduler (batch/transform): completion within target window 95% of the time; SLO 99.0% success for scheduled jobs.
- Logging ingestion (log-forwarder): < 60s ingestion latency for 99% of events; SLO 99.5%.

Dashboards (recommended set):
- Platform overview dashboard (single pane): aggregated errors, top 10 services by error rate, control plane latency p50/p90/p99, cluster capacity utilization, and active incidents.
- Inference routing dashboard: per-model QPS, p50/p90/p99 latency, tail latency trend, KV cache hit rate, ongoing batching sizes, and model fallback count.
- Alert heatmap: alerts by service and severity for last 24h/7d.
- CI/CD pipeline health: queue length, avg duration, failing job rate, and infra provisioning delays.
- Observability pipeline: log volume, ingestion errors, Prometheus scrape health, and tracing sampling rate.

Dashboard panels and example queries (Datadog/Prometheus examples):
- Control plane 5m error rate (PromQL): sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane",code!~"2.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane"}[5m]))
- Ingress p99 latency (Histogram): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ingress_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service))
- KV cache hit rate: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])))

Alerting guidance and thresholds (platform defaults):
- Sev P0 (page and Slack): partial outage impacting >25% of customers or control plane down. Trigger: control plane availability < 99.5% in 5m window OR ingress error rate > 10% across regional frontends.
- Sev P1 (urgent, page to oncall): latency p99 > 2x baseline AND user-facing errors > 1% sustained for 5m.
- Sev P2 (notify in Slack, email): background job failures > 5% over rolling 30m or CI pipeline failure rate increases > 10% from baseline.
- Blackbox heartbeat: missing heartbeat for core services for 3 consecutive minutes triggers an immediate page.

Alert-to-runbook mapping (required):
- Every alert MUST include a link to a runbook that covers: detection, mitigation steps, rollback/kill steps, communication templates, owner, and post-incident next steps.
- Example: ingress-high-error-rate -> runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/ingress-high-error-rate.

Canonical runbook template (confluence-friendly):
1. Title and owners
2. Symptoms / how alert appears
3. Impact assessment (what is affected)
4. Quick mitigation steps (what to run immediately)
5. Diagnostic steps (logs, queries, dashboards)
6. Recovery and verification steps
7. Rollback / mitigation checklist
8. Post-incident tasks and owners
9. Related pages and runbooks

Example condensed runbook: Ingress high 5xx error rate
- Owners: eng-platform / ingress subteam
- Symptoms: spike in 5xxs on ingress-health panel, top upstream showing connection refused
- Mitigation steps:
  1. Set routing fallback to model-variant B: curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/v1/route/fallback -d '{"variant":"A-compat"}'
  2. Scale ingress deployment to +3 replicas: kubectl scale deployment ingress --replicas=$(($(kubectl get deploy ingress -o jsonpath='{.status.replicas}') + 3))
  3. Temporarily raise circuit-breaker threshold: edit ConfigMap / platform-config/circuit-breakers
- Diagnostics:
  - kubectl logs -n platform ingress-<pod> | grep ERROR
  - Datadog: query ingress.errors{service:ingress}.rollup(sum, 300)
- Recovery verification: p99 latency returns to baseline and error-rate below 0.5% for 10m

How-tos (common procedures):
- Add a new dashboard: use the dashboard template -> name with service prefix (platform-<service>-overview), include at least: SLI panels, traffic panels, error panels, and a link to its runbook. Submit PR to dashboards repo and tag @observability-team for review.
- Add an alert: create alert in Datadog/Prometheus with a playbook link, set severity, and add owner. Must include a runbook before unmuting.
- Onboard a new service: checklist:
  1. Create service entry in service-registry (owner, contact, repo).
  2. Add metrics: request_total, request_errors_total, request_duration_seconds histogram, cpu/memory saturation metrics.
  3. Add traces: instrument top-level request path and critical backend calls.
  4. Create dashboard and runbook.
  5. Add to CI smoke tests and deployment gating.

Retrospective highlights (last 3 retros):
- Incident: control-plane config rollout 2025-11-09 -> root cause: config validation gap in the rollout job; action: add schema validation step to the rollout pipeline and a canary rollout policy.
- Incident: logging pipeline lag 2025-12-20 -> root cause: downstream consumer backpressure; action: add backpressure metrics, consumer autoscaling guide, and 10% headroom target in pipeline capacity planning.
- Incident: model fallback cascade 2026-01-12 -> root cause: missing quota enforcement on per-tenant inference; action: add tenant rate limiters and end-to-end test for fallback path.

Roadmap (next 6 months priorities):
- Q2 2026:
  1. Observability expansion: add per-tenant cost-by-feature dashboards and integrate anomaly detection for sudden cost spikes. Owner: eng-platform / observability.
  2. Canary automation: finish rollout orchestration to support automated percentage-based canaries with built-in health checks. Owner: infra.
  3. Runbook automation: wire alerts to create incident tasks automatically and capture runbook checklists in the incident timeline. Owner: ops-tools.
- Q3 2026:
  1. Platform autoscaling: advanced cluster autoscaler tuned for batched inference workloads.
  2. Unified tracing sampling: reduce noise and ensure 10% end-to-end sampling for critical paths.

Retrospective process (how we improve):
- After every Sev P0/P1 incident we run a 2-week blameless retro, assign corrective actions, and track them in the platform roadmap board.
- Quarterly reliability review: assess SLO burn, error budget consumption, and top three reliability initiatives.

Runbook maintenance and lifecycle:
- Owners must review runbooks quarterly or after any incident where the runbook was used.
- Deprecated runbooks: mark with label 'deprecated' and link to replacement.

Communication templates (short):
- Incident start (channel): "[INCIDENT] {short-summary} — Impact: {customers affected}. Oncall: {name}. Updates every 15m"
- Customer update (email): include incident summary, ETA for fix, mitigation in place, and next steps.

Appendix: helpful commands and playbook snippets
- Get pod logs: kubectl -n platform logs -l app=ingress --tail=500
- Restart deployment: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<name> -n platform
- Temporarily mute alert in Datadog: datadog api suppression create --scope "service:ingress" --message "temporary mute for mitigation"

Document maintenance:
- This doc is maintained by eng-platform. Please propose edits via the standard Confluence edit flow and add reviewers @Miguel Torres and @Aisha Patel for major changes.

If you are oncall and this is your first time responding: follow the runbook template above, notify the incident lead, and escalate to the platform lead after 30 minutes if the mitigation is not stabilizing the system.
